Performers
Artur Schnabel (piano) Documented

The Archive description, selected file’s artist tag and Bloesch’s discography agree. Bloesch’s session list identifies a Bechstein piano; no instrument serial number is established.

[1] [4] [3]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The solo-piano work is identified, but Schnabel’s performing edition and any editorial alterations are not. The listening commentary uses the viewable original edition, plate 521, as a score source, not as a claimed identification of the edition used in the session. No cut or take-splice history is supplied for this MP3.

[1] [4] [7]
Recorded
1933-04-11 Documented

The Op. 57 description specifies 11.IV.1933, corroborated by the discography and reissue documentation. The Archive item’s general date of 1932 covers the compilation and is not this sonata’s session date. The embedded date tag 2001 is not treated as a session or transfer date.

[1] [4] [5]
Place
Abbey Road Studios, Studio No. 3, London, England Documented

Bloesch’s chronological session list gives Studio No. 3 and a Bechstein piano; the alphabetical work entry gives Abbey Road Studios, London.

[4] [5]
Label
Unknown Unknown

The original commercial issue was His Master’s Voice. The label of the physical carrier or later reissue actually used to make this MP3 is not identified; original-issue information is not substituted for transfer provenance.

[1] [4] [3]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

Bloesch identifies the original complete-sonata issue as HMV DB 2215–⁠2217 in Beethoven Sonata Society Volume 5, part of set DB 2211–⁠2217. The transferred pressing or reissue catalogue number is unknown. The embedded portrait contains no readable carrier identification.

[4] [6] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

Original session documentation assigns movement I to two sides, 2B 6605 and 2B 6606, with takes 2 listed as the issued masters; the catalogue lists 2B 6605II and 2B 6606II. These identify the historical issued recording, not an independently verified take selection or side-join position in the selected MP3.

[4] [6] [1]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or restoration engineer is credited for this file. The Archive uploader recordplayer78 is not equated with an engineer or owner. Andrew Rose’s credit on the separately consulted Pristine reissue is not transferred to this MP3; no upstream link to that reissue is established.

[1] [2] [3] [5]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive added/public date is 27 March 2020. The embedded date tag is 2001, without an identified release or transfer to which it refers. Neither date establishes when the analogue source was transferred or restored.

[1] [3]
Processing
The MP3’s encoder tag states ‘Audiograbber 1.83.01, LAME dll 3.99, 256 Kbit/s, Joint Stereo, Normal quality’. Documented

Inspection of the downloaded selected stream found MP3 audio at 44,100 Hz, two channels and 256,000 bit/s, plus an attached JPEG portrait. Two-channel encoding is not evidence of an original stereo session. Analogue transfer equipment, equalisation, noise reduction, pitch/speed correction, restoration and edit history remain unknown. Archive calls the file ‘VBR MP3’; that repository format label is distinct from the inspected stream and encoder tag.

[3] [1]
Composition rights
The underlying Beethoven composition is public domain under the ordinary EU life-plus-70 term. Inferred, not documented

Beethoven died in 1827. The cited original score contains the historical composition; no unidentified modern performing edition is cleared by this term calculation. Composition rights are separate from the rights in Schnabel’s recording.

[6] [10] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: original sound recording first published in 1934. Documented

The Public Domain Project release-set catalogue explicitly gives 1934 as the first release of HMV DB 2211–⁠2217; Bloesch identifies Op. 57 within that issue as DB 2215–⁠2217, matrices 2B 6605–⁠6610. Publication is thus documented separately from the 11 April 1933 session. Under the programme’s territorial EU rule, the earlier 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. US status is not established and no worldwide clearance is claimed. The Archive’s Public Domain Mark is an assertion, not an ownership release; the Public Domain Project’s worldwide/US expiry table is not relied upon. No CC licence or independently established additional rights in an unidentified modern transfer are asserted.

Ludwig van Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 23, Op. 57, I. Allegro assai — Artur Schnabel, piano; recorded 11 April 1933, Abbey Road Studio No. 3, London. Originally issued by HMV in Beethoven Sonata Society Volume 5; selected MP3 supplied through Internet Archive item beethovenschnabel6. Transfer engineer and transferred carrier unknown. Territorial EU recording basis; US status not established. Rights statement
